headline: Voting is your formal voice—the mechanism that translates individual preference into collective decision
universal_truth: Your vote is small individually but essential collectively; democracy works when people participate
fun_facts: Many elections have been decided by tiny margins—sometimes a handful of votes
Voter turnout varies enormously—from over 90% in some countries to under 40% in others
People fought and died for voting rights that many now take for granted
discussion_questions: Do you vote regularly? Why or why not?
How do you decide who to vote for?

hook.script: One voice among millions—does it matter? Your vote alone rarely decides anything. But democracy isn't about one vote deciding; it's about everyone's voice counting. Voting is how preference becomes policy.

cliff.script: One vote rarely changes outcomes. So why bother voting?

options.text: Voting matters collectively, not individually—if everyone thought their vote didn't matter, democracy would collapse; voting is citizenship in action, not just personal calculus
options.response: Yes. Democracy is a collective action problem. Each vote is small, but together they create mandate. Your vote matters because enough people voting is how democracy works at all.
Expression is part of it, but voting is more than feeling—it's participating in actual decisions...

fact1.title: Informed Voting
fact1.script: Voting without information is noise, not signal. Know what you're voting on. Research candidates and issues. An informed vote contributes more than an uninformed one.

fact2.title: Barriers to Voting
fact2.script: Not everyone can vote easily. Registration, access, time off work—barriers exist. Some are practical; some are deliberate. Removing barriers strengthens democracy.

fact3.title: Beyond Elections
fact3.script: Voting happens beyond elections: in organizations, communities, informal groups. The skill of participating in collective decisions applies everywhere. Practice it.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Your vote is small individually but essential collectively. Democracy works when people participate. Use your voice.

outro.script: That's Day 334—November complete! Tomorrow begins December, and we'll explore how groups make rules. Until then, consider how you use your voice.

growTrack.title: Voting Commitment - Will You Use Your Voice?
growTrack.activity: Do you vote regularly? Are you registered? Do you research before voting? Make a commitment: What will you do to ensure you're an informed, participating voter?
